# Fixed audio samples

CODING_STANDARDS section 9: the scoring integration tests run against fixed
samples rather than generated bytes, so a score that changes means the code
changed.

| file | content |
|---|---|
| `drill_short.wav` | 0.25 s, 220 Hz tone, 8 kHz mono PCM |
| `drill_long.wav` | 0.5 s, 330 Hz tone — a different length, so FakeScorer gives it a different (still stable) score |
| `silence.wav` | 0.2 s of digital silence |

These are synthetic tones, not speech. FakeScorer derives its scores from
`reference_text` and `len(audio)` (ARCHITECTURE 3.2), so speech would buy
nothing today — and the files stay small enough to live in the repository.

**Do not regenerate them.** A real scorer arrives with M0-1 (BACKLOG E9), and
at that point these are replaced by recordings of the good/bad sample pairs
M0-1 collects. Until then their only job is to be identical on every machine.
